## Avocado pudding

This stuff tastes good, and you can pretend your being healthy.

**Source:** Source: I think a friend posted it on Facebook and I looked it up once. May have been from [TheKitchn](https://www.thekitchn.com/how-to-make-the-best-chocolate-avocado-pudding-239245).


**Ingredients:**


```{r}
#| label: avocado-pudding

dat <- tibble(
  Ingredients = c(
    "1 ripe avocado",
    "1-2 tsp cocoa powder",
    "1 tsp honey"
  ),
  spcr1 = " ",
  Tools = c(
    "Bowl for mixing",
    "Fork and/or spoon",
    ""
  )
)


colnames(dat)[str_detect(colnames(dat), "spcr")] <- ""

dat |> 
  tt(  theme = "striped" ) |> 
  style_tt(fontsize = 0.8) |> 
  style_tt( i=0, background=bgcol, color="white")


```



**Directions:**

1. Do what you do to get the meat of the avocado out. I usually slice it in quarters to be able to peel the skin off.
2. You may want to cut it up as much as possible with a knfe.
3. Start mashing it. This is 95% of the work. Get it to a very smooth consistency. You might have other tools to do this better, I don’t.
4. Mix in the cocoa powder and honey. Once it’s mixed in well, take a sample. Add more cocoa powder and honey as desired.


**Variations:**

- Adding a bit of cinnamon might give this a Mexican chocolate taste. I haven’t tried it yet, but now I want to.


**Notes:**

- The avocado really needs to be ripe. You want to make sure it gets really mashed up, no chunks.
- The measurements are approximate, I usually go towards the high end, or maybe even a bit more.
